transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood CSM), Michael Ortiz (BaysideBank), Priya Narang (BaysideBank Security), Evan Liu (Bayside Product)

Summary: quick POC weekly to go over security/compliance items: SSO setup, audit logs schema and retention, SOC2 evidence, key management (KMS/HSM), and next steps for pilot. Short perf notes but mostly security.

Topics: SSO (Okta/SAML/SCIM), audit log fields & export, data retention & deletion API, SOC2 and pen test artifacts, customer-managed keys / HSM, VPC/private deployment options, RBAC/entitlements

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we can get started. Uh, quick check on attendees - we have Priya, Michael, Evan from Bayside and Laura and Jordan from Redwood, correct?
[00:12] Michael: Yep that's right. Thanks Samir.
[00:15] Priya: Hi, yep I'm on. We wanted to focus this week mostly on the SSO flow and the audit logs retention question.
[00:22] Laura: Great, we can do that. Quick reminder — our earlier note, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, and we also have an Okta integration template. The demo will show SSO -> provisioning -> role sync.
[00:36] Priya: Sounds good. One of our constraints: we need all admin actions to be logged and retained for at least 7 years for certain workflows, and we need export into our Splunk/SIEM.
[00:48] Jordan: Quick note, we do provide an audit log export. By default pilot retention is 90 days, but for enterprise accounts we can configure longer retention or stream logs to your S3 or directly to your SIEM via syslog/SF (transcription: s-f?) connector.
[01:03] Michael: Right that 90 days default is fine for the POC, but for production we'll need the 7 years. How does Redwood support customer-managed retention policies and egress?
[01:13] Laura: Two paths: 1) Hosted with extended retention — we can change TTL and store logs in a hardened bucket with lifecycle rules, or 2) Stream logs out in real time to your SIEM or your S3 and you control retention there. For extremely strict customers we recommend the private deployment where logs never leave your VPC.
[01:31] Priya: OK. For the POC we want to validate the SIEM export and confirm what fields are present. Specifically we need user principal, action type, object id, request headers, IP, client id, session id, and the request/response hashes for auditability. Are those available?
[01:47] Laura: We emit a standard audit schema: timestamp, user, action, resource, result (success/fail), request_id, ip, user_agent. We can add extra fields on request like headers or hashes; some of the header content may be redacted by default. I will double-check the exact field names and share a sample JSON schema.
[02:03] Priya: Please do. Also is the audit log tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody for certain investigations.
[02:12] Samir: Good question. We support HMAC signing of log batches for the hosted product and also write a checksum to a separate journaling store — again for the highest assurance we recommend streaming logs into your own immutable store (S3 with Object Lock or your SIEM that supports WORM).
[02:28] Priya: That helps. Next SSO: we plan to use Okta, SAML-based. We also want SCIM provisioning so groups and roles map. What level of RBAC granularity can we sync?
[02:40] Laura: SCIM supports groups to roles mapping. We have role templates and you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles like admin, developer, reader. For finer-grained entitlements we support attribute-based mappings as well. The provisioning delta is near real-time during the POC.
[02:56] Evan: For audit purposes we also need admin approvals for role elevation. Does Redwood have an approval workflow out-of-the-box?
[03:03] Laura: Not as a built-in approval queue today; we recommend integrating with your internal workflows or using our API to trigger an approval flow in your ticketing system. That said, you can require 2-person approval via an intermediate step in SCIM provisioning if needed — it's a configuration we can discuss with product ops.
[03:20] Michael: On encryption — we need both at-rest and in-transit. Also, customer-managed keys are a requirement for us in prod. How do you handle CMKs / HSM?
[03:30] Samir: We support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and for private deployments we can integrate with HSMs. Keys can be rotated on your schedule and you can set key access policies. For hosted we currently offer envelope encryption with CMK control for data at rest.
[03:46] Priya: Do you store KV cache or any model intermediate state that could be considered sensitive?
[03:52] Laura: We store KV cache for inference performance but by default it's encrypted at rest and is scoped per customer. For private deployments, the KV cache stays inside your VPC. Also, we have a cache purge API so you can periodically evict or set TTLs.
[04:07] Priya: Good. Another ask: we need a data deletion API so we can run subject access requests and delete customer-provided PII from the pilot data store. Is that available?
[04:17] Laura: Yes — deletion API exists; it marks data for purge and we have background jobs that remove artifacts. For pilot the SLA is 48 hours, for enterprise we can contract shorter windows. We'll share the API spec.
[04:30] Priya: Please include the retention/eraser endpoint and sample flows for SAR.
[04:35] Samir: Noted.
[04:37] Michael: SOC2 — can you confirm Redwood's current status? We need copies of the SOC2 Type II report and your last pen test summary for our procurement team.
[04:46] Samir: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II as of Q2 2026. I'll share the report and a summarized pen test. We'll also include our control matrix and any compensating controls. You'll have redacted vendor info in the report — if you need unredacted we can handle via an NDA.
[05:00] Priya: Great, we'll need those by Monday for the security review.
[05:04] Samir: I'll upload them to the deal folder and send a link after the call.
[05:08] Evan: For the pilot we're also testing a private deployment on a small VM to simulate our air-gapped network for a subset of sensitive calls — is that still available?
[05:17] Laura: Yes we have a lightweight private bundle for proofs: it runs in your VPC with a customer-controlled control plane. It requires a small ops runbook; we typically do a joint install with the infra team. For POC it's a limited footprint.
[05:30] Michael: Do you have a checklist for network requirements? We need to know ports, egress endpoints, and whether we need peering vs private link.
[05:38] Laura: We'll share the network diagram and a minimal ports list. For peering we support VPC peering and PrivateLink; choice depends on your network posture. We'll include guidance for firewall rules.
[05:48] Priya: One more — audit trail access: can we pull logs via API or do we need the export?
[05:54] Jordan: You can pull via audit API for recent logs and we also support streaming to your SIEM for long-term storage.
[06:00] Priya: Ok good.
[06:03] Samir: Quick recap and next steps: I'll share SOC2 and pen test, Laura will do SSO demo and send sample audit schema, Priya will share compliance control list. Anything else?
[06:14] Michael: We'll validate timeline internally and get back on the 7-year retention question for prod. For now we'll proceed with SIEM export test.
[06:23] Evan: Also, can we get a sample of the audit log JSON so our security team can map fields to Splunk?
[06:28] Laura: Yes, will attach sample JSON in the follow-up.
[06:31] Samir: Great — we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.
[06:35] Priya: Thanks, bye.
